source_snapshot.procedure: Check the test-item information, collect evidence and confirm the information remains correct after reboot.
source_snapshot.criteria: Information is correct and remains correct after reboot.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek greps Cache Speed from Type 7 output without cache-record identity, expected values or the required post-reboot collection, and incorrectly describes filtered text as full raw output.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify the SMBIOS Type 7 Cache Speed byte for every owner-required cache record against the platform cache map and confirm the same values remain correct after reboot.
original_test_intent.target: Every applicable SMBIOS Type 7 Cache Information structure, mapped by structure handle, Socket Designation, Cache Configuration level and Type 4 processor-cache handles to the correct processor/cache instance.
original_test_intent.scope: Read the descriptive firmware field `Cache Speed` before and after one approved reboot. Under DMTF SMBIOS 3.9.0 this byte is cache module speed in nanoseconds and zero means unknown; it is not a runtime cache clock or performance benchmark.
original_test_intent.operation: Capture complete Type 4/Type 7 and platform identity, map every required cache handle, decode/preserve each Cache Speed byte in nanoseconds, compare it with the owner-approved per-cache value or approved Unknown policy, obtain reboot approval, repeat the same mapping and comparison, and verify boot/management health.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: Two read-only collections separated by one approved reboot; no performance workload or extra iteration is specified.
original_test_intent.expected_result: All required Type 7 cache records are present and unambiguously linked to the expected processor/cache level, every Cache Speed byte matches the approved nanosecond value or explicitly approved zero/Unknown policy before and after reboot, and platform health returns normally.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: SUT/CPU/BIOS/SMBIOS and dmidecode versions, owner per-handle/socket/level Cache Speed matrix in nanoseconds, complete pre/post Type 4 and Type 7 structures, extracted raw/decoded values, stable handle mapping, exact comparison, reboot timeline and host/BMC health.
ambiguities: The source supplies no expected per-cache speed or policy for SMBIOS zero/Unknown.
It does not define which Type 7 records and processor/cache links apply on a multi-socket server.
The procedure omits the explicit reboot step required by its persistence criterion.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly requires every cache handle/level, complete output, expected values and an approved reboot. It leaves units/encoding and descriptive-versus-runtime semantics as owner choices even though DMTF defines the field as nanoseconds with zero meaning Unknown, and its optional runtime frequency check can conflate a firmware access-time descriptor with live cache clock/performance.

applicable_history.decision: The historical record accepts a Type 7 dmidecode query but provides only a grep fragment and delegates correctness/persistence without a cache map.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Retain the hybrid classification for package/spec/reboot dependencies. V3 fixes the field semantics to DMTF nanoseconds/zero-is-Unknown, requires Type 4-to-Type 7 instance mapping and removes the unrelated runtime-frequency interpretation.

available_now: DMTF SMBIOS 3.9.0 defines Type 7 Cache Speed at offset 0Fh as a one-byte nanosecond value, with zero meaning Unknown.
Pre-reboot Type 4/Type 7 structures can be collected safely before the owner baseline is available.
The source requires persistence but no cache performance workload or configuration change.
missing_inputs: Expected Cache Speed byte/value in nanoseconds for every applicable cache handle/socket/level, or explicit acceptance of zero/Unknown
Authoritative CPU/socket/cache topology and Type 4-to-Type 7 mapping for the exact SUT recipe
Validated dmidecode package/sudo/host access, reboot approval/workload isolation, stable power and OOB recovery
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform/BIOS owner supplies the per-cache SMBIOS expectation and Unknown policy; the CPU/platform owner confirms topology mapping; the lab/system owner supplies tooling/access and approves the reboot/recovery window.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect dmidecode/SMBIOS versions and complete `dmidecode -t 4 -t 7` data without filtering or clearing logs

Build a provisional table of Type 4 processor handles and their L1/L2/L3 Cache Handles plus each Type 7 handle, designation, configuration level, installed size and Cache Speed, marking acceptance pending
prohibited_until_closed: Do not declare PASS from non-empty grep output, choose one cache record, convert nanoseconds into a runtime clock claim, run an unrelated performance test or accept zero as correct without owner policy
Do not modify CPU/cache/firmware settings, reboot without approval/OOB recovery, clear logs or discard missing/duplicate/unlinked records
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Every required Type 7 handle maps to the correct CPU/cache role and one owner-approved nanosecond byte/value or Unknown policy; dmidecode/access are validated; reboot/recovery are approved; identical parsing and mapping can run pre/post reboot.

revision_candidate.purpose: Verify the DMTF-defined Type 7 Cache Speed value for every required cache record and confirm the mapped values remain correct after one reboot.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact multi-socket CPU/server recipe and BIOS/SMBIOS build with an approved Type 4/Type 7 cache map, validated dmidecode, host access, reboot window and BMC/OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All required Type 7 structures, mapped by handle/designation/configuration level and Type 4 L1/L2/L3 handle references. Interpret Cache Speed only as the SMBIOS byte in nanoseconds; zero is Unknown.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Per-cache expected nanosecond value or approved Unknown policy; CPU/socket/cache and Type 4/Type 7 map; dmidecode version/package and sudo access; SUT credentials; reboot approval, workload isolation, power/OOB recovery and evidence destination.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Collect complete pre-reboot Type 4 and Type 7 output and map all required caches; preserve and compare each Cache Speed raw/decoded nanosecond value; after explicit approval reboot once; repeat the identical collection/mapping/comparison and verify host/BMC health.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct SUT/CPU/BIOS selected; expected cache map and values signed; dmidecode validated; least-privilege host access available; workload quiesced; reboot window, power and OOB recovery ready; logs preserved.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Signed per-cache matrix; SUT/CPU/BIOS/SMBIOS/dmidecode identity; unfiltered pre/post Type 4 and Type 7 output; handle/link table; raw and decoded nanosecond values; comparison results; reboot timeline; OS/BMC health and exceptions.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: DMTF DSP0134 SMBIOS 3.9.0 Type 7 Cache Speed encoding plus the exact platform/CPU/BIOS specification supplying the expected value for each cache instance.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Use read-only SMBIOS queries only. Do not alter CPU/cache/firmware settings, infer frequency/performance from the field, accept zero without policy, omit cache instances, clear logs or reboot without approval and recovery.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Platform owner supplies/accepts the cache matrix and Unknown policy; system/workload owner approves reboot and resolves mismatches. Ordinary pre-reboot read-only collection needs no additional approval.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners provide platform expectations and authorize reboot. Once supplied, collection, handle mapping, byte decoding, comparison and approved reboot orchestration can be automated.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: If reboot or management recovery fails, stop and use approved console/BMC/OOB recovery. On missing, duplicate, unknown or changed cache records, preserve complete dumps and firmware context and do not change performance/firmware settings under this case.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Missing expected cache map/value policy, unresolved Type 4/Type 7 links, incomplete/invalid output, unapproved zero/Unknown, pre-test mismatch, missing reboot approval/recovery, boot/management failure or any post-reboot handle/value drift.

identified_defects: DeepSeek loses cache identity and never performs the required reboot comparison.
V2 treats DMTF-defined nanosecond encoding as unresolved and allows an unrelated runtime-frequency interpretation.
The source lacks a multi-socket per-cache map and expected zero/Unknown policy.
reason_for_change: Anchor the test to the actual SMBIOS byte semantics and prevent a runtime-frequency or single-cache proxy from replacing the required per-record firmware metadata persistence check.

new_technical_evidence.title: DMTF DSP0134 SMBIOS Specification
new_technical_evidence.applicability: SMBIOS Type 7 structures; actual SUT SMBIOS version must be recorded
new_technical_evidence.supports: Type 7 offset 0Fh Cache Speed is a BYTE expressing cache module speed in nanoseconds, and value 0 means unknown; Cache Configuration encodes the cache level used for record mapping.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The platform-specific expected byte/value and Type 4/Type 7 topology are absent from the source.

removed_ambiguities: Fixes units to nanoseconds and zero semantics to Unknown.
Removes the unrelated live frequency/performance branch.
Requires every Type 7 instance to be linked to its CPU/cache role before comparison.
resolved_blockers: DMTF resolves field encoding; expected values are still owner inputs but do not prevent safe actual-value collection.
remaining_blockers: PASS and reboot remain blocked until per-cache expected values/Unknown policy, topology map, tooling/access, approval and recovery are ready.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 replaces an open-ended runtime-frequency interpretation with the authoritative DMTF nanosecond byte semantics, adds Type 4 link-based instance mapping and keeps the required pre/post reboot comparison fully read-only.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The corrected nanosecond semantics and multi-cache mapping are queued for isolated validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source checks SMBIOS Type 7 Cache Speed correctness and requires the information to remain correct after reboot.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 adds per-cache/reboot evidence but leaves a DMTF-defined nanosecond field open to an unrelated runtime-frequency interpretation.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Collect and map every Type 7 record read-only, compare its nanosecond byte to owner policy and reboot only with approval/OOB recovery; never tune cache/CPU settings or substitute a benchmark.
